analysis.title: GS - Pasquariello - Markets - Macro - 31 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 57 bps on the week (the equal-weight S&P rose 80 bps), but this masks heavy single-stock, sector and thematic rotation underneath the index.

October combined a small index move with difficult risk management. This continues a pattern through the second half of 2026: S&P monthly returns of -0.13% (Jul), +2.62% (Aug), -0.45% (Sep), -0.93% (Oct), against GSPRHIMO momentum basket returns of -30.19%, -13.67%, +26.96% and -18.60%.
Pasquariello's base view: the primary bull trend remains intact, but the market will deliver less upside power and sub-surface volatility is here to stay. He is not making big bets right now.

Q3 tech earnings were dominated by disappointment despite a few cloud businesses compounding high growth on large bases. Hyperscaler capex intentions are not slowing, but several large companies missed in the core of their business.

He expects the bull market to continue in 2027 with less punch. S&P earnings have been superb, but earnings growth appears to have peaked and the rate of upgrades to forward estimates has slowed versus recent reporting cycles.

For the next two months he sees technicals favoring the bulls: sentiment is clearly downbeat, the seasonal swing runs from the weakest stretch (mid-Aug to mid-Oct) to the strongest (mid-Oct to year-end), and the market has cleared a lot of length over the past month. The bear counterpoint is that the same was said into late 2018.
The Fed meeting this week was uneventful and barely discussed by equity traders.
Tension between oil and European equities: crude (COZ6) is at its highs on a risk premium built into the midterms, while European equities rose again and the Swiss SMI hit record highs.
He agrees with increasing commodity allocation. BCOM is +28% YTD and GS recently published both a tactical and a structural bull case.

US mega cap tech has been very weak over the past three weeks. The 4th largest company in the index just had its worst single day as a public company, while the broader trend in S&P ex-AI was charted.
